items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: like Dexter Gordon and Charlie Mingus and Ornette Coleman, and on and on. But those were all Los Angeles players.

ctx.x: So you’ve never done the New York thing?

No. I spent a lot of time in New York. I’ve never actually resided there. I’ve been there for weeks at a time on different recording projects or playing. I’ve always regretted that and I always advise young players if they’re really serious about doing something, sooner or later they have to deal with New York. They have to take that step and do it. And that discourages a lot of them right there. But I firmly believe that New York is the proving ground where ultimately you have to be able to hold your own, if…

those things anywhere, virtually, if it’s an area of any size. But if you’re serious about carving a place for yourself in the scheme of things, it has to be done in New York City. And it doesn’t happen in Los Angeles, and it doesn’t happen — now people can, once they’ve arrived in New York, can go anywhere and carry that attaché with them. I mean I know great New York players who now live in Santa Fe, New Mexico or wherever, but they will always be thought of as New York players. It doesn’t matter. But if you…
